claim: Focal seizures start with low-voltage fast activity, evolve into rhythmic burst discharges and are followed by a period of suppressed background activity.
source: Human and animal EEG data demonstrate that focal seizures start with low-voltage fast activity, evolve into rhythmic burst discharges and are followed by a period of suppressed background activity.
evidence: The claim is supported by reference to human and animal EEG data, indicating empirical observations from experimental studies.

claim: Processes with dynamics in the range of tens of seconds govern focal seizure evolution.
source: This suggests that processes with dynamics in the range of tens of seconds govern focal seizure evolution.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that seizures evolve through distinct phases over tens of seconds.

claim: The computational model closely replicates the electrographic pattern of a typical human focal seizure characterized by low voltage fast activity onset, tonic phase, clonic phase and postictal suppression.
source: Our biophysically realistic computational model closely replicates the electrographic pattern of a typical human focal seizure characterized by low voltage fast activity onset, tonic phase, clonic phase and postictal suppression.
evidence: The claim is supported by the computational model results presented in the manuscript.

claim: Seizure initiation can occur via inhibitory interneurons through the initial build-up of extracellular K+ due to intense interneuronal spiking.
source: Our study demonstrates, for the first time in silico, the potential mechanism of seizure initiation by inhibitory interneurons via the initial build-up of extracellular K+ due to intense interneuronal spiking.
evidence: The claim is demonstrated through computational modeling results.

claim: Ionic mechanisms underlie progressive slowing down of ictal discharges towards the end of seizure.
source: The model also identifies ionic mechanisms that may underlie a key feature in seizure dynamics, that is, progressive slowing down of ictal discharges towards the end of seizure.
evidence: The claim is supported by model predictions and analysis.

claim: Inter-burst intervals exhibit specific scaling patterns during seizure termination.
source: Our model prediction of specific scaling of inter-burst intervals is confirmed by seizure data recorded in the whole guinea pig brain in vitro and in humans, suggesting that the observed termination pattern may hold across different species.
evidence: The claim is supported by both model predictions and experimental validation in guinea pig and human data.

claim: Ionic dynamics are elementary processes behind seizure generation.
source: Our results emphasize ionic dynamics as elementary processes behind seizure generation and indicate targets for new therapeutic strategies.
evidence: The claim is based on the overall findings of the computational model and experimental validation.

claim: Low-voltage fast (LVF) activity in the gamma range (30–80 Hz) is a frequently observed onset pattern in patients with temporal lobe epilepsy.
source: A frequently observed onset pattern in patients with temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) is characterized by low-voltage fast (LVF) activity in the gamma range (30–80 Hz) (Avoli et al., 2016; de Curtis and Gnatkovsky, 2009; Lagarde et al., 2019; Perucca et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to published research.

claim: LVF seizure onset is followed by recruitment of irregular spiking behavior which evolves into periodic burst discharges that gradually decrease in frequency and suddenly cease.
source: LVF seizure onset is followed by the recruitment of irregular spiking behavior which evolves into periodic burst discharges that gradually decrease in frequency and suddenly cease.
evidence: The claim describes observed seizure progression patterns.

claim: Seizures are often followed by a period of reduced EEG amplitude known as postictal EEG suppression.
source: Seizures are often followed by a period of reduced EEG amplitude known as postictal EEG suppression.
evidence: The claim describes a well-known clinical observation.

claim: Blocking synaptic transmission via a low Ca2+ solution led to the development of synchronized seizure-like events in hippocampal CA1 slices.
source: It has been shown that blocking synaptic transmission via a low Ca2+ solution led to the development of synchronized seizure-like events (SLE) in hippocampal CA1 slices (Jefferys and Haas, 1982; Yaari et al., 1983) and in the intact hippocampus (Feng and Durand, 2003).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to experimental studies.

claim: Synchronized epileptiform activity can be recorded across two hippocampal regions separated by a mechanical lesion, without the involvement of electrochemical synaptic communication.
source: Moreover, the synchronized epileptiform activity can be recorded across two hippocampal regions separated by a mechanical lesion, without the involvement of electrochemical synaptic communication (Lian et al., 2001).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to an experimental study.

claim: In photosensitive baboons, light-induced neocortical seizure discharges were accompanied by depletion of extracellular Ca2+ to levels incompatible with chemical synaptic transmission.
source: Finally, in photosensitive baboons, light-induced neocortical seizure discharges were accompanied by depletion of extracellular Ca2+ to levels incompatible with the chemical synaptic transmission (Pumain et al., 1985).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to an experimental study.

claim: A paradoxical increase in inhibitory cell firing and a decrease in pyramidal cell activity at seizure onset was documented in in vitro rodent slices.
source: Additionally, a paradoxical increase in inhibitory cell firing and a decrease in pyramidal cell activity at seizure onset was documented in in vitro rodent slices (Derchansky et al., 2008; Fujiwara-Tsukamoto et al., 2007; Lévesque et al., 2016; Lillis et al., 2012; Ziburkus et al., 2006), in the in vitro whole guinea pig brain (Gnatkovsky et al., 2008; Uva et al., 2015), and in human and animal in vivo recordings (Elahian et al., 2018; Grasse et al., 2013; Miri et al., 2018; Toyoda et al., 2015; Truccolo et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to experimental studies across different preparations.

claim: Processes at the network level related to changes in synaptic gains cannot be the sole mechanisms that control seizure generation and progression.
source: The above-mentioned studies suggest that processes at the network level related to changes in synaptic gains cannot be the sole mechanisms that control seizure generation and progression, and that other factors must be involved in the process of ictogenesis.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the cited experimental evidence showing seizures can occur without normal synaptic transmission.

claim: The model consisted of five cells, four pyramidal neurons (PY) and a fast-spiking inhibitory interneuron (IN), arranged as a chain structure.
source: The model consisted of five cells, four pyramidal neurons (PY) and a fast-spiking inhibitory interneuron (IN), arranged as a chain structure (Figure 1).
evidence: The claim describes the model architecture shown in Figure 1.

claim: The ionic dynamics of K+, Na+, Ca2+, and Cl− were incorporated and activity-dependent changes in their concentrations were computed.
source: The ionic dynamics of K+, Na+, Ca2+, and Cl− were incorporated and activity-dependent changes in their concentrations were computed.
evidence: The claim describes a key feature of the computational model.

claim: Brief perfusion (3 min) of 50 microM bicuculline in the isolated guinea pig brain transiently reduces GABAergic inhibition to 60–70% and leads to strong interneuron bursting in the absence of principal cells activity.
source: Brief perfusion (3 min) of 50 microM bicuculline in the isolated guinea pig brain transiently reduces GABAergic inhibition to 60–70% and leads to strong interneuron bursting in the absence of principal cells activity (Gnatkovsky et al., 2008; Uva et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to experimental studies.

claim: Strong firing (initial rate of 150 Hz) of the IN led to small amplitude fast activity in the LFP signal associated with the onset of the simulated SLE.
source: Strong firing (initial rate of 150 Hz) of the IN (Figure 2C) led to small amplitude fast activity in the LFP signal (Figure 2A between the 60 and 68 s timestamps) associated with the onset of the simulated SLE.
evidence: The claim is supported by the simulation results shown in Figure 2.

claim: After approximately 10 s, the PY cells began to generate a strong tonic discharge, resulting in an irregular LFP spiking signal with increased amplitude typically associated with the SLE tonic phase.
source: After approximately 10 s, the PY cells began to generate a strong tonic discharge, resulting in an irregular LFP spiking signal with increased amplitude typically associated with the SLE tonic phase (Figure 2B; 65–80 s).
evidence: The claim is supported by the simulation results shown in Figure 2.

claim: Approximately 20 s after the onset of the SLE, the cellular firing pattern of PY cells switched from tonic to bursting discharge.
source: Approximately 20 s after the onset of the SLE, the cellular firing pattern of PY cells switched from tonic to bursting discharge, leading to LFP oscillations which corresponded to the bursting phase (Figure 2A, after 80 s).
evidence: The claim is supported by the simulation results shown in Figure 2.

claim: As the SLE progressed, the burst rate gradually decreased and ictal discharges spontaneously terminated.
source: As the SLE progressed, the burst rate gradually decreased and ictal discharges spontaneously terminated.
evidence: The claim describes the model behavior during seizure termination.

claim: The SLE was followed by a period of silence for approximately 90 s which was visible in the LFP signal and in the PY and IN traces.
source: Postictally, the SLE was followed by a period of silence for approximately 90 s which was visible in the LFP signal and in the PY and IN traces (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by the simulation results shown in Figure 2.

claim: At the onset of the seizure, extracellular potassium concentration ([K+]o) increased sharply in the somatic compartment, remained elevated throughout the SLE and slightly decreased toward the end of the episode.
source: At the onset of the seizure, extracellular potassium concentration ([K+]o) increased sharply in the somatic compartment, remained elevated throughout the SLE and slightly decreased toward the end of the episode (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by the simulation results shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Intracellular sodium concentration ([Na+]i) steadily increased during the bursting phase in both somatic and dendritic compartments and reached a plateau around the offset of the SLE.
source: Intracellular sodium concentration ([Na+]i) steadily increased during the bursting phase in both somatic and dendritic compartments and reached a plateau around the offset of the SLE (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is supported by the simulation results shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Intracellular chloride concentration ([Cl-]i) exhibited a gradual increase from the beginning of the SLE and was highest at the end of the paroxysmal firing.
source: Intracellular chloride concentration ([Cl-]i) exhibited a gradual increase from the beginning of the SLE and was highest at the end of the paroxysmal firing (Figure 2F).
evidence: The claim is supported by the simulation results shown in Figure 2F.

claim: In the isolated guinea pig brain, the SLE activity with an LVF onset pattern was induced by 3 min arterial application of bicuculine.
source: In the isolated guinea pig brain, the SLE activity with an LVF onset pattern (Figure 3A, top trace) was induced by 3 min arterial application of bicuculine.
evidence: The claim describes the experimental protocol used to induce seizures in the guinea pig brain preparation.

claim: The transition from preictal to ictal state was associated with a strong discharge of fast-spiking interneurons and transient silencing of the PY cells.
source: The transition from preictal to ictal state which occurred at approximately second 10 was associated with a strong discharge of fast-spiking interneurons (Figure 3A, third trace) and transient silencing of the PY cells (Figure 3A, second trace).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: [K+]o sharply increased at the onset of the SLE and remained elevated afterward in the guinea pig brain preparation.
source: [K+]o sharply increased at the onset of the SLE and remained elevated afterward (Figure 3A, bottom trace).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The in silico results replicated the experimental data in many respects including LFP signal characteristics, cellular firing pattern and [K+]o time course.
source: The in silico results (shown for comparison in the same timescale in Figure 3B) replicated the experimental data in many respects including LFP signal characteristics, cellular firing pattern and [K+]o time course.
evidence: The claim compares model results with experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: An increase in [K+]o reduces the driving force of K+ currents responsible for hyperpolarized resting membrane potential and spike repolarization.
source: For example, an increase in [K+]o reduces the driving force of K+ currents responsible for hyperpolarized resting membrane potential and spike repolarization.
evidence: The claim is based on established biophysical principles.

claim: [Cl-]i accumulation causes depolarizing shift in EGABAa reducing the efficacy of GABAa inhibition.
source: [Cl-]i accumulation causes depolarizing shift in EGABAa reducing the efficacy of GABAa inhibition.
evidence: The claim is based on established biophysical principles.

claim: Accumulation of [K+]o and [Na+]i increases the pump rate and enhances the hyperpolarizing pump current.
source: Accumulation of [K+]o and [Na+]i increases the pump rate and enhances the hyperpolarizing pump current.
evidence: The claim is based on the known properties of the Na+/K+-pump.

claim: The main effect of an increase in [Na+]i was a shrinking of the tonic and bursting domains and an expansion of the resting domain due to upregulation of the hyperpolarizing effect of increased [Na+]i on the pump current.
source: A comparison of the network activities for different values of [Na+]i in the three graphs in Figure 4A demonstrates that the main effect of an increase in [Na+]i was a shrinking of the tonic and bursting domains and an expansion of the resting domain due to upregulation of the hyperpolarizing effect of increased [Na+]i on the pump current.
evidence: The claim is supported by the bifurcation analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: A sharp increase in [K+]o,soma led to a transition from rest to tonic firing.
source: The initial increase of somatic [K+]o (stage I) led to a transition from the resting state to tonic firing (Figure 4A, first panel)
evidence: The claim is supported by the bifurcation analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: A subsequent increase in dendritic [K+]o led to a transition from tonic firing to bursting.
source: while a subsequent increase in dendritic [K+]o (stage II) led to a transition from tonic firing to bursting (Figure 4A, middle panel).
evidence: The claim is supported by the bifurcation analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: A subsequent decrease in somatic and dendritic [K+]o led to the termination of the SLE, as the cell activity reentered the resting state region.
source: A subsequent decrease in somatic and dendritic [K+]o (stage III) led to the termination of the SLE, as the cell activity reentered the resting state region (Figure 4A, last panel).
evidence: The claim is supported by the bifurcation analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: When chloride accumulation was removed, the firing of the interneuron exerted a steady inhibitory influence on the PY cells and the bursting SLE phase was not manifested.
source: When chloride accumulation was removed (Figure 5A), the reversal potentials of the Cl- and GABAa currents (ECl and EGABAa) were fixed (blue and light blue lines in Figure 5A, second panel). Under such conditions, the firing of the interneuron (Figure 5A, third panel) exerted a steady inhibitory influence on the PY cells. Additionally, it increased [K+]o above fixed [Cl-]i level (Figure 5A, fourth panel). As a result, EK exceeded ECl and the KCC2 transported K+ and Cl- into the cells (Figure 5A, fifth panel) and reduced the external K+ concentration. All these effects transiently increased the PY cells tonic firing but the bursting SLE phase was not manifested (Figure 5A, first and second panel).
evidence: The claim is supported by the simulation results shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Activation of the IN in the reference model, with chloride dynamics intact, led to a typical SLE.
source: Conversely, activation of the IN in the reference model, with chloride dynamics intact, led to a typical SLE (Figure 5B, top panel).
evidence: The claim is supported by the simulation results shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The [Cl-]i accumulation was dominated by Cl- influx through GABAa receptors and to lesser degree by KCC2 cotransport.
source: The [Cl-]i accumulation was dominated by Cl- influx through GABAa receptors and to lesser degree by KCC2 cotransport (Figure 5B, fifth and bottom panel).
evidence: The claim is supported by the simulation results shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Chloride accumulation led to enhanced excitability by increasing the chloride reversal potential toward the PY membrane potential, reducing the hyperpolarizing chloride leak current.
source: It led to enhanced excitability in two ways: (i) by increasing the chloride reversal potential (blue line in Figure 5B, second panel) toward the PY membrane potential, reducing the hyperpolarizing chloride leak current
evidence: The claim is supported by the simulation results shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Chloride accumulation led to enhanced excitability by increasing the GABAa reversal potential that approached the PY cell membrane potential, reducing the postsynaptic inhibitory current.
source: (ii) by increasing the GABAa reversal potential (Figure 5B, second panel, light blue) that approached the PY cell membrane potential, reducing the postsynaptic inhibitory current.
evidence: The claim is supported by the simulation results shown in Figure 5B.

claim: A gradual increase in the interval between ictal bursts (IBI) was visible in the model.
source: In the model, a gradual increase in the interval between ictal bursts (IBI) was visible (Figures 2A and 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by the simulation results shown in Figures 2A and 3B.

claim: The IBI on the semi-log graph laid on a straight line suggesting an exponential relationship.
source: The IBI on the semi-log graph laid on a straight line suggesting an exponential relationship.
evidence: The claim is based on the analysis of IBI evolution shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The evolution of the IBI during an SLE in a whole-brain in vitro preparation and a human TLE seizure exhibited the same characteristics as the model.
source: The evolution of the IBI during an SLE in a whole-brain in vitro preparation (Figure 6B) and a human TLE seizure (Figure 6C) exhibited the same characteristics.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 6B and 6C.

claim: The exponential fit always had the lowest RMSE in the experimental data.
source: In the experimental data the exponential fit always had the lowest RMSE.
evidence: The claim is based on the quantitative analysis of IBI fits.

claim: Linear decrease in [K+]o led to exponential IBI evolution.
source: Linear decrease in [K+]o led to exponential IBI evolution, while linear increase in [Na+]i or decrease in [Cl-]i led to SLE termination with logarithmic scaling of IBI as determined by RMSE (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by the fast-slow system analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Slowing of inter-burst interval towards the end of an SLE is mediated by simultaneous changes in [K+]o and [Na+]i in the model.
source: These results suggest that in the model, slowing of inter-burst interval towards the end of an SLE is mediated by simultaneous changes in [K+]o and [Na+]i.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the analysis of separate ion contributions to IBI slowing.

claim: After the termination of an SLE there was an approximate 90-s period during which firing was either absent or reduced with respect to the interictal period.
source: As shown in Figure 2A–C, after the termination of an SLE there was an approximate 90-s period during which firing was either absent or reduced with respect to the interictal period.
evidence: The claim is supported by the simulation results shown in Figure 2.

claim: Shortly after termination of the SLE, burst responses were still triggered, however, after few seconds, the excitability decreased and remained reduced for approximately 90 s.
source: Our results showed that shortly after termination of the SLE, burst responses were still triggered, however, after few seconds, the excitability decreased and remained reduced for approximately 90 s (Figure 7B).
evidence: The claim is supported by the stimulation protocol results shown in Figure 7B.

claim: The high excitability immediately after termination of the SLE was correlated with elevated [K+]o which was present shortly after the SLE.
source: The high excitability immediately after termination of the SLE (timestamps between seconds 110 and 125) was correlated with elevated [K+]o which was present shortly after the SLE (Figure 7C).
evidence: The claim is supported by the simulation results shown in Figure 7C.

claim: The subsequent postictal reduction of excitability was associated with decay of [K+]o and an increased hyperpolarizing Na+/K+-pump current in somatic and dendritic compartments.
source: The subsequent postictal reduction of excitability was associated with decay of [K+]o and an increased hyperpolarizing Na+/K+-pump current in somatic and dendritic compartments.
evidence: The claim is supported by the simulation results shown in Figure 7.

claim: The pump current decayed with a slower time constant associated with a gradual clearance of [Na+]i by the pump.
source: The pump current decayed with a slower time constant associated with a gradual clearance of [Na+]i by the pump (Figure 7DE).
evidence: The claim is supported by the simulation results shown in Figure 7DE.

claim: Seizures with LVF onset are initiated by discharges of fast-spiking GABAergic interneurons.
source: There is increasing evidence showing that seizures with LVF onset are initiated by discharges of fast-spiking GABAergic interneurons (de Curtis and Avoli, 2016; de Curtis and Gnatkovsky, 2009; Devinsky et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published research.

claim: Increased interneuron discharges and decreased PY activity around the time of seizure onset were first evidenced in in vitro and in vivo animal models.
source: Increased interneuron discharges and decreased PY activity around the time of seizure onset were first evidenced in in vitro and in vivo animal models (Gnatkovsky et al., 2008; Grasse et al., 2013; Lévesque et al., 2016; Lopantsev and Avoli, 1998; Miri et al., 2018; Toyoda et al., 2015; Ziburkus et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to experimental studies.

claim: A similar scenario was observed with single-unit recordings performed during intracerebral presurgical monitoring in neocortical and temporal lobe epilepsy patients.
source: A similar scenario was observed with single-unit recordings performed during intracerebral presurgical monitoring in neocortical and temporal lobe epilepsy patients (Elahian et al., 2018; Truccolo et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to clinical studies.

claim: Causal relationship between increased interneuron firing and ictogenesis may include intracellular chloride accumulation resulting in a shift in EGABAa and/or the elevation of [K+]o.
source: Causal relationship between increased interneuron firing and ictogenesis may include intracellular chloride accumulation resulting in a shift in EGABAa and/or the elevation of [K+]o, which leads to subsequent depolarization of PY cells and seizure development (Magloire et al., 2019b).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to published research.

claim: The hypothesis that seizure initiation is related to an elevation in [K+]o caused by a strong initial discharge has been tested in computational models with ion concentration changes.
source: The hypothesis suggested by Jensen and Yaari, 1997 that seizure initiation is related to an elevation in [K+]o caused by a strong initial discharge has been tested in computational models with ion concentration changes.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to published research.

claim: In these simulations, seizure-like activity has been induced by DC stimulation of the PY cells alone, by a brief increase in [K+]o, by stimulation of the IN and PY cells or by varying the extracellular concentration of K+ and O2.
source: In these simulations, seizure-like activity has been induced by DC stimulation of the PY cells alone (Bazhenov et al., 2004; Buchin et al., 2016; Kager et al., 2002), by a brief increase in [K+]o (Fröhlich et al., 2006), by stimulation of the IN and PY cells (Y Ho and Truccolo, 2016) or by varying the extracellular concentration of K+ and O2 (Wei et al., 2014b).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to computational modeling studies.

claim: Transitions to spontaneous seizures that begin with LFV pattern were not associated with increased excitatory activity, but with increased firing of inhibitory interneurons.
source: However, as mentioned above, transitions to spontaneous seizures that begin with LFV pattern were not associated with increased excitatory activity, but with increased firing of inhibitory interneurons.
evidence: The claim is based on the experimental evidence discussed earlier in the manuscript.

claim: Pyramidal cell – interneuron interplay during SLE was first investigated in the computational model of Wei et al., 2014a which mimicked 4-aminopyridine (4-AP) and decreased magnesium in vitro conditions.
source: Pyramidal cell – interneuron interplay during SLE was first investigated in the computational model of Wei et al., 2014a which mimicked 4-aminopyridine (4-AP) and decreased magnesium in vitro conditions (Ziburkus et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a computational modeling study.

claim: When potassium diffusion rate around the IN was lower than around the PY cell, the IN depolarized and increased its activity and eventually entered depolarization block giving way to the strong firing of the PY cell during an SLE.
source: They showed that when potassium diffusion rate around the IN was lower than around the PY cell, the IN depolarized and increased its activity and eventually entered depolarization block giving way to the strong firing of the PY cell during an SLE.
evidence: The claim describes findings from the Wei et al., 2014a model.

claim: An increase in interneuron firing triggered a transition to a self-sustained SLE during which both IN and PY cells were active simultaneously.
source: We demonstrated that an increase in interneuron firing triggered a transition to a self-sustained SLE during which both IN and PY cells were active simultaneously.
evidence: The claim describes findings from the authors' previous work (Gentiletti et al., 2017).

claim: González et al., 2018 showed that interneuron stimulation by current pulses led to the development of an SLE via a gradual increase in [K+]o mediated by the KCC2 cotransporter.
source: González et al., 2018 showed that interneuron stimulation by current pulses led to the development of an SLE via a gradual increase in [K+]o mediated by the KCC2 cotransporter.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a computational modeling study.

claim: Activation of GABAa receptors led to an increase in [K+]o and cell depolarization, which were eliminated by the KCC2 inhibitor, furosemide.
source: This hypothesis is supported by in vitro experiments which showed that activation of GABAa receptors led to an increase in [K+]o and cell depolarization, which were eliminated by the KCC2 inhibitor, furosemide (Viitanen et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to an experimental study.

claim: The application of the KCC2 blockers VU0240551 and bumetanide prevented SLEs during 4-AP application in rat brain slices.
source: The above-mentioned hypothesis is also consistent with the findings that the application of the KCC2 blockers VU0240551 and bumetanide prevented SLEs during 4-AP application in rat brain slices (Hamidi and Avoli, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to an experimental study.

claim: In the pilocarpine model, the enhancement of KCC2 in principal cortical neurons is associated with a reduction in seizure duration.
source: In the pilocarpine model, the enhancement of KCC2 in principal cortical neurons is associated with a reduction in seizure duration (Magloire et al., 2019a).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to an experimental study.

claim: KCC2 activity does not affect seizure initiation, but influences seizure maintenance during a prolonged period of Cl- accumulation.
source: Based on these results, the authors suggested that KCC2 activity does not affect seizure initiation, but influences seizure maintenance during a prolonged period of Cl- accumulation.
evidence: The claim is based on the interpretation of results from Magloire et al., 2019a.

claim: KCC2 potentiation delayed the onset of an SLE after 4-AP application in vitro and reduced the severity of kainate-induced seizures in vivo.
source: The antiepileptic role of enhanced KCC2 activity has also been suggested by Moore et al., 2018, who showed that KCC2 potentiation delayed the onset of an SLE after 4-AP application in vitro and reduced the severity of kainate-induced seizures in vivo.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to an experimental study.

claim: Under normal conditions, when [K+]o is sufficiently controlled by homeostatic mechanisms, GABAergic activity leads to the extrusion of Cl- and K+ by KCC2.
source: Under normal conditions, when [K+]o is sufficiently controlled by homeostatic mechanisms, GABAergic activity leads to the extrusion of Cl- and K+ by KCC2.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about KCC2 function.

claim: An increase in [K+]o may reverse the K+–Cl- cotransport, thus contributing to [K+]o buffering rather than accumulation.
source: However, an increase in [K+]o may reverse the K+–Cl- cotransport, thus contributing to [K+]o buffering rather than accumulation (Payne, 1997; Thompson and Gahwiler, 1989)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published research.

claim: The activation of IN in the model led to a rapid increase in [K+]o in the narrow extracellular interstitial compartments, while intracellular Cl- accumulation was more gradual.
source: The activation of IN in our model led to a rapid increase in [K+]o in the narrow extracellular interstitial compartments, while intracellular Cl- accumulation was more gradual (Figure 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by the simulation results shown in Figure 2.

claim: This generated an influx of K+ and Cl- via KCC2, which led to [K+]o buffering and [Cl-]i accumulation.
source: This generated an influx of K+ and Cl- via KCC2 (Figure 5B), which led to [K+]o buffering and [Cl-]i accumulation.
evidence: The claim is supported by the simulation results shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The primary mechanism of [K+]o accumulation in the model was due to other processes, such as the outward K+ current that repolarizes action potentials in activated IN and PY cells.
source: The exclusion of KCC2 involvement in the increase in [K+]o suggests that the primary mechanism of [K+]o accumulation in our model was due to other processes, such as the outward K+ current that repolarizes action potentials in activated IN and PY cells.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the model analysis showing KCC2 did not contribute to K+ accumulation.

claim: A significant local [K+]o rise due to increased spiking activity following electrical stimulation of the cat cerebral cortex was observed.
source: This observation is consistent with in vivo experimental evidence that showed a significant local [K+]o rise due to increased spiking activity following electrical stimulation of the cat cerebral cortex (Heinemann and Lux, 1975).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to an experimental study.

claim: In the model KCC2 resumes extruding Cl- shortly after SLE termination.
source: It is worth noting that in our model KCC2 resumes extruding Cl- shortly after SLE termination (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by the simulation results shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Intracellular chloride imaging during SLE induced in vitro by Mg2+-free solution showed that [Cl-]i started to decline before the end of SLE.
source: Intracellular chloride imaging during SLE induced in vitro by Mg2+-free solution showed that [Cl-]i started to decline before the end of SLE (Raimondo et al., 2013)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to an experimental study.

claim: During SLE induced in vivo by 4-AP [Cl-]i recovery begun instantly after SLE offset.
source: while during SLE induced in vivo by 4-AP [Cl-]i recovery begun instantly after SLE offset (Sulis Sato et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to an experimental study.

claim: The initial fast rise of [K+]o in the somatic compartment and slower rise in dendritic segment was related to the localisation of inhibitory neuron near the PY soma.
source: The initial fast rise of [K+]o in the somatic compartment and slower rise in dendritic segment (Figure 2D) was related to the localisation of inhibitory neuron near the PY soma.
evidence: The claim is based on the model architecture and simulation results.

claim: During paroxysmal firing induced by electrical stimulation, [K+]o in dentate gyrus reached significantly higher levels in cell body layers than in the layers containing dendrites.
source: This model prediction appears to agree with experimental data of simultaneous recordings of [K+]o in somatic and dendritic layers during hippocampal seizures in anesthetized rats. During paroxysmal firing induced by electrical stimulation, [K+]o in dentate gyrus reached significantly higher levels in cell body layers than in the layers containing dendrites (Somjen and Giacchino, 1985).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to an experimental study.

claim: High [K+]o in the soma and moderately increased [K+]o in dendrites favored burst firing through the reduction of repolarizing K+ currents, the activation of a Na+ persistent current, and a shift from spike after-hyperpolarization toward depolarizing after-potentials.
source: High [K+]o in the soma and moderately increased [K+]o in dendrites favored burst firing (Figure 4A and Appendix 1—figure 1) through the reduction of repolarizing K+ currents, the activation of a Na+ persistent current, and a shift from spike after-hyperpolarization toward depolarizing after-potentials.
evidence: The claim is based on the bifurcation analysis and model mechanisms.

claim: Prolonged depolarization led to the activation of slow M-type K+ conductance, which hyperpolarized the PY cells after a series of fast spikes.
source: Prolonged depolarization led to the activation of slow M-type K+ conductance (Appendix 1—figure 2), which hyperpolarized the PY cells after a series of fast spikes.
evidence: The claim is based on the model mechanisms shown in Appendix 1—figure 2.

claim: The bursting mechanism in the model originated from currents used in the original entorhinal cortex cells model and was similar to the mechanism in CA1 neurons.
source: The bursting mechanism in our model originated from currents used in the original entorhinal cortex cells model (Fransen et al., 2002) and was similar to the mechanism in CA1 neurons (Golomb et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published models.

claim: A transition from resting to tonic and then to bursting activity in PY cells was not critically dependent on perisomatic inhibition and would be also observed if dendrite-targeting, SST interneurons were simulated.
source: We note that in our model a transition from resting to tonic and then to bursting activity in PY cells was not critically dependent on perisomatic inhibition and would be also observed if we simulated dendrite-targeting, SST interneurons.
evidence: The claim is based on the bifurcation analysis showing transitions can occur with either somatic or dendritic K+ increases.

claim: Optogenetic activation of either PV or SST inhibitory interneurons can trigger SLE.
source: This observation is in agreement with the study showing that optogenetic activation of either PV or SST inhibitory interneurons can trigger SLE (Yekhlef et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to an experimental study.

claim: In the model, the SLE terminated spontaneously.
source: In our model, the SLE terminated spontaneously.
evidence: The claim describes a key feature of the model behavior.

claim: SLE cessation in the model can be explained by two coincident factors, namely the decrease in [K+]o during stable levels of increased [Na+]i.
source: This indicates that SLE cessation in the model can be explained by two coincident factors, namely the decrease in [K+]o during stable levels of increased [Na+]i.
evidence: The claim is based on the fast-slow analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: An increase in [Na+]i led to an increased hyperpolarizing Na+/K+-pump current, which increased the firing threshold in the neurons.
source: An increase in [Na+]i led to an increased hyperpolarizing Na+/K+-pump current, which increased the firing threshold in the neurons.
evidence: The claim is based on the known properties of the Na+/K+-pump and model behavior.

claim: The increased pump activity also contributed to a progressive decrease in [K+]o.
source: The increased pump activity also contributed to a progressive decrease in [K+]o.
evidence: The claim is based on the model mechanisms.

claim: Potassium repolarization currents increased after each burst and eventually prevented the initiation of a new cycle of the oscillation.
source: Potassium repolarization currents increased after each burst and eventually prevented the initiation of a new cycle of the oscillation.
evidence: The claim is based on the model mechanisms underlying seizure termination.

claim: The idea that negative feedback between [Na+]i accumulation and neuronal firing is responsible for seizure termination was first formulated by Jensen and Yaari, 1997.
source: The idea that negative feedback between [Na+]i accumulation and neuronal firing is responsible for seizure termination was first formulated by Jensen and Yaari, 1997.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to published research.

claim: The inhibition of Na+/K+-pump activity occurring during hypoxia prolongs SLE discharges and shortens post-SLE period in hippocampal slices with blocked synaptic transmission.
source: Even though it has not been tested experimentally, this hypothesis is consistent with the observation that the inhibition of Na+/K+-pump activity occurring during hypoxia prolongs SLE discharges and shortens post-SLE period in hippocampal slices with blocked synaptic transmission (Haas and Jefferys, 1984).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to an experimental study.

claim: A decrease in Na+ channel conductance via the antiepileptic drug phenytoin, increased the seizure threshold but prolonged the afterdischarges and seizure durations in the rat kindling model of epilepsy.
source: It was also observed that a decrease in Na+ channel conductance via the antiepileptic drug phenytoin, increased the seizure threshold but prolonged the afterdischarges and seizure durations in the rat kindling model of epilepsy (Ebert et al., 1997).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to an experimental study.

claim: In the computational model developed by the Bazhenov team and Chizhov et al., 2018, a progressive increase in [Na+]i and activation of the electrogenic Na+/K+-pump were identified as the primary factor of SLE termination.
source: In the computational model developed by the Bazhenov team (Krishnan et al., 2015; Krishnan and Bazhenov, 2011) and Chizhov et al., 2018, a progressive increase in [Na+]i and activation of the electrogenic Na+/K+-pump were identified as the primary factor of SLE termination.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to computational modeling studies.

claim: The seizure termination mechanism in the above-mentioned studies is similar to the mechanism observed in the present study.
source: The seizure termination mechanism in the above-mentioned studies is similar to the mechanism observed in the present study, even though different specifications of neuronal mechanisms, network characteristics and seizure morphologies were used.
evidence: The claim compares the current model with previous models.

claim: Saggio et al., 2020 analyzed frequency slowing in human focal onset seizures and estimated that approximately 40% exhibited unequivocal discharge slowing down toward the end.
source: Saggio et al., 2020 analyzed frequency slowing in human focal onset seizures and estimated that approximately 40% exhibited unequivocal discharge slowing down toward the end.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a clinical study.

claim: Burst frequency slowing was confirmed in a study on the entorhinal cortex of the isolated brain preparation during bicuculline- and 4AP-induced SLE.
source: Burst frequency slowing was confirmed in a study on the entorhinal cortex of the isolated brain preparation during bicuculline- and 4AP-induced SLE (Boido et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to an experimental study.

claim: Inter-burst intervals in focal epilepsy patients were predominantly described by the exponential scaling law.
source: These findings are also consistent with those of Bauer et al., 2017, which demonstrated that inter-burst intervals in focal epilepsy patients were predominantly described by the exponential scaling law.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a clinical study.

claim: Depending on the bifurcation which leads to seizure termination, the burst oscillation frequency can be constant or decrease according to the logarithmic or square root relationship.
source: Conversely, it has been suggested that depending on the bifurcation which leads to seizure termination, the burst oscillation frequency can be constant or decrease according to the logarithmic or square root relationship (Izhikevich, 2000; Jirsa et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to theoretical studies.

claim: This theory has not been confirmed by the model and experimental seizure data.
source: This theory has not been confirmed by our model and experimental seizure data (Figure 6).
evidence: The claim is based on the comparison of model and experimental results with theoretical predictions.

claim: In the model, progressive decrease in neuronal excitability related to simultaneous decrease in [K+]o and increase in [Na+]i, was responsible for the IBI slowing toward an SLE end.
source: In our model, progressive decrease in neuronal excitability related to simultaneous decrease in [K+]o and increase in [Na+]i, was responsible for the IBI slowing toward an SLE end.
evidence: The claim is based on the model analysis of IBI slowing mechanisms.

claim: Bauer et al., 2017 included a plasticity parameter that progressively decoupled spatially distributed neural mass units based on the synchrony level.
source: Bauer et al., 2017 included a plasticity parameter that progressively decoupled spatially distributed neural mass units based on the synchrony level.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a computational modeling study.

claim: This mechanism accounted for seizure termination, exponential IBI increase and the presence of a transient postictal state.
source: This mechanism accounted for seizure termination, exponential IBI increase and the presence of a transient postictal state.
evidence: The claim describes findings from Bauer et al., 2017.

claim: In the model of Liou et al., 2020 the IBI was constant during seizure expansion and only when the spatial propagation of ictal discharge ceased, the seizure entered the pre-termination stage with a slowing-down trend.
source: In the model of Liou et al., 2020 the IBI was constant during seizure expansion and only when the spatial propagation of ictal discharge ceased, the seizure entered the pre-termination stage with a slowing-down trend.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a computational modeling study.

claim: An increase in the IBI in the pre-termination phase was related to the recovery of inhibition and restoration of the Cl- concentration gradient.
source: An increase in the IBI in this phase was related to the recovery of inhibition and restoration of the Cl- concentration gradient.
evidence: The claim describes findings from Liou et al., 2020.

claim: Spatial properties related to seizure propagation and synchrony are other factors that may affect the evolution of the IBI.
source: These studies indicate that spatial properties related to seizure propagation and synchrony are other factors that may affect the evolution of the IBI.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the discussion of alternative models.

claim: Seizures are followed by the suppression of physiological rhythms known as postictal EEG suppression (PES) that lasts for seconds or minutes.
source: Seizures are followed by the suppression of physiological rhythms known as postictal EEG suppression (PES) that lasts for seconds or minutes (Pottkämper et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to published research.

claim: The PES duration in the model is consistent with a typical 'seconds to minutes' timescale.
source: The PES duration in our model is consistent with a typical 'seconds to minutes' timescale although available estimates depend on the PES duration assessment method.
evidence: The claim compares model results with clinical observations.

claim: In single-unit recordings in epileptic patients with neocortical seizures neuronal spiking was fully suppressed for 5–30 s after seizure termination.
source: In single-unit recordings in epileptic patients with neocortical seizures neuronal spiking was fully suppressed for 5–30 s after seizure termination (Truccolo et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a clinical study.

claim: Average duration of postictal suppression based on EEG features in focal seizure patients was estimated at 17 s, 120 s and around 50–100 s in different studies.
source: Average duration of postictal suppression based on EEG features in focal seizure patients was estimated at 17 s (Grigorovsky et al., 2020; Table 1), 120 s (Payne et al., 2018; Table 1) and around 50–100 s (Bauer et al., 2017; Figure 5).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to clinical studies.

claim: The in silico-derived prediction that postictal 'silence' depends on the increased rate of hyperpolarizing Na+/K+-pump has been previously suggested and simulated.
source: Our in silico-derived prediction that postictal 'silence' depends on the increased rate of hyperpolarizing Na+/K+-pump has been previously suggested (Fisher and Schachter, 2000) and simulated (Krishnan et al., 2015; Krishnan and Bazhenov, 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published research.

claim: In these models, postictal state was generated via both, reduced [K+]o to below baseline level and increased [Na+]i after termination of an SLE.
source: In these models, postictal state was generated via both, reduced [K+]o to below baseline level and increased [Na+]i after termination of an SLE.
evidence: The claim describes findings from previous computational models.

claim: [K+]o decrease below baseline resulted in a negative shift in EK and membrane hyperpolarization, while elevated [Na+]i increased Na+/K+-pump hyperpolarizing current.
source: [K+]o decrease below baseline resulted in a negative shift in EK and membrane hyperpolarization, while elevated [Na+]i increased Na+/K+-pump hyperpolarizing current.
evidence: The claim describes mechanisms from previous computational models.

claim: A below-reference value of [K+]o was indeed observed after seizure termination.
source: A below-reference value of [K+]o was indeed observed after seizure termination (Heinemann et al., 1977).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to an experimental study.

claim: In other studies, [K+]o decayed to baseline level after an SLE offset and couldn't contribute to the postictal state.
source: On the other hand, in other studies, [K+]o decayed to baseline level after an SLE offset (Fisher et al., 1976; Futamachi et al., 1974) and couldn't contribute to the postictal state.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to experimental studies.

claim: In the model [K+]o undershoot was not observed, suggesting that the main cause of postictal reduction in excitability was hyperpolarizing effect of the Na+/K+-pump current.
source: Also in our model [K+]o undershoot was not observed (Figure 7C), suggesting that the main cause of postictal reduction in excitability was hyperpolarizing effect of the Na+/K+-pump current, which remained elevated above baseline for about 100 s after SLE termination (Figure 7DE).
evidence: The claim is based on the simulation results shown in Figure 7.

claim: Ion homeostatic processes activated and sustained by the excessive seizure discharges provide a negative feedback mechanism, eventually leading to the cessation of the seizure itself and to the restoration of the normal state after a transitional period of postictal silence.
source: The findings generated by our computational model suggest that ion homeostatic processes activated and sustained by the excessive seizure discharges provide a negative feedback mechanism, eventually leading to the cessation of the seizure itself and to the restoration of the normal state after a transitional period of postictal silence.
evidence: The claim summarizes the main conclusion from the model results.
